If \(f(x)\) is a quadratic polynomial such that \(f(0)=3\), \(f'(2)=2\) and \(f'(3)=12\) then find \(f(x)\).
If \(f(x)=a\sin x-b\cos x\), \(f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sqrt{2}\) and \(f'\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=2\), then find \(f(x)\).

_note: BOOK DEFECT (typesetting). As printed the radical bar in the stem covers 'x + 2', i.e. \(\sqrt{x+2}\) — verified by pixel measurement of the vinculum (spans the whole of x + 2, 72 px, against the 22 px vinculum the same book uses for \(\sqrt{x}\) elsewhere on the page, e.g. Ex 9.2 IV Q2). Option B carries the same over-wide bar; option D's bar correctly covers only x. Under the printed reading \(\frac{d}{dx}\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{x+2}}=\frac{x+8}{2(x+2)^{3/2}}\), which matches NO option, so the question is unanswerable as printed. The evidently-intended stem is \(y=\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{x}+2}\): then \(x-4=(\sqrt{x}-2)(\sqrt{x}+2)\) so \(y=\sqrt{x}-2\) and \(\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) = option C, which is exactly option C as printed. Answer C is derived from that intended reading; the stem and option B are transcribed as printed, not repaired.
solution: [Textbook misprint in the stem, answer-affecting as printed: the radical bar overshoots to cover \(x + 2\). Measured on the page, the stem's vinculum spans 72 px, covering the \(x\), the \(+\) and the \(2\), against the same book's ordinary \(\sqrt{x}\) at 22 px elsewhere on the same page. As printed the derivative of \(\dfrac{x-4}{\sqrt{x+2}}\) is \(\dfrac{x+8}{2(x+2)^{3/2}}\), which matches NO option, so the question is unanswerable. The intended stem is \(\dfrac{x-4}{\sqrt{x}+2}\), which factors as \(\dfrac{\left(\sqrt{x}-2\right)\left(\sqrt{x}+2\right)}{\sqrt{x}+2} = \sqrt{x} - 2\) and differentiates to \(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) — the keyed option. The answer above follows the intended reading. Note the option set straddles both readings, which is presumably how the ambiguity arose.]

stem: Suppose \(f(x)\) is the derivative of \(g(x)\) and \(g(x)\) is the derivative of \(h(x)\). If \(h(x)=a\sin x+b\cos x+c\) then \(f(x)+h(x)=\)
_note: Option D is printed as \(-2(a\sin + b\cos x)\) — the first term's 'sin' carries no argument (the book has dropped the x). Transcribed exactly as printed. It is a distractor either way and does not affect the answer.
solution: [Textbook misprint in an option: the alternative printed as \(-2\left(a\sin + b\cos x\right)\) has the argument of the first \(\sin\) dropped, so it is not a well-formed expression. The key is unaffected — the correct value is \(c\), which a different alternative carries, so this is a malformed distractor and not in contention.]

stem:
If \(f(x)=2x+6\) for \(0\le x\le 2\)
\(=ax^{2}+bx\) for \(2<x\le 4\)
is differentiable at \(x=2\) then the values of \(a\) and \(b\) are.

options.label: A
options.text: f is continuous at \(x=0\), but not differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: B
options.text: f is neither continuous nor differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: C
options.text: f is not continuous at \(x=0\), but differentiable at \(x=0\)

options.label: D
options.text: f is both continuous and differentiable at \(x=0\)

_note: BOOK DEFECT. The condition \(x\le 0\) is printed TWICE, once for each branch (verified on the page image at 2x zoom). As printed the definition is self-contradictory — it assigns two different values to every \(x\le 0\) and leaves \(f\) undefined for \(x>0\) — so the question has no answer. The evidently-intended second condition is \(x>0\). Transcribed exactly as printed, NOT repaired. The answer is derived from the intended reading: at \(x=0\) the left value is \(0+0+1=1\) and the right value is \(0-0+1=1\), so \(f\) is continuous; \(Lf'(0)=\left[2x+\cos x\right]_{x=0}=1\) while \(Rf'(0)=\left[2x-2\right]_{x=0}=-2\), so \(f\) is not differentiable at \(x=0\) — option A.
solution: [Textbook misprint in the stem: the piecewise function prints the SAME condition on both branches — \(= x^2 + \sin x + 1\) for \(x \le 0\) and \(= x^2 - 2x + 1\) for \(x \le 0\). As printed the function is doubly defined on \(x \le 0\) and undefined for \(x > 0\), so it cannot be what is intended; the second branch must read \(x > 0\). Under that reading both branches give \(1\) at \(x = 0\), so \(f\) is continuous there, while the left derivative \(2x + \cos x \to 1\) and the right derivative \(2x - 2 \to -2\) differ, so \(f\) is not differentiable — which is the keyed answer.]

Determine whether the following function is differentiable at \(x=3\) where,

\(=6x-7\), for \(x<3\).

\(f(x)=3-x\), for \(x<1\)
\(=px^{2}+qx\), for \(x\ge 1\).

Determine the values of \(p\) and \(q\) that make the function \(f(x)\) differentiable on \(R\) where
\(f(x)=px^{3}\), for \(x<2\)
\(=x^{2}+q\), for \(x\ge 2\).

Determine all real values of \(p\) and \(q\) that ensure the function
\(f(x)=px+q\) for, \(x\le 1\)
\(=\tan\left(\frac{\pi x}{4}\right)\), for \(1<x<2\)
is differentiable at \(x=1\).
